drug_class: Atypical Antipsychotic (also called a second-generation antipsychotic)
purpose: Aripiprazole is used to help treat conditions like schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and depression (when added to an antidepressant). It can also help reduce irritability in people with autism. Your doctor may prescribe it to help stabilize your mood, reduce hallucinations or unusual thoughts, or help you feel more balanced overall.
how_it_works: Your brain uses chemical messengers called dopamine and serotonin to communicate. In some mental health conditions, these chemicals are out of balance. Aripiprazole works by partially blocking or activating certain receptors for these chemicals, helping to bring them back into a healthier balance. Think of it like a dimmer switch — it turns things up or down depending on what your brain needs.
common_side_effects: Some people notice feeling restless or having trouble sitting still (called akathisia), drowsiness, headache, nausea, dizziness, weight gain, or blurred vision. Some people also notice an increased appetite. These effects are often mild and may get better after the first few weeks.
warnings: Important: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor first — stopping too quickly can cause your symptoms to come back. Tell your doctor right away if you feel very restless, have uncontrolled movements, or notice changes in blood sugar levels. Elderly patients with dementia should use extra caution, as this drug carries a serious risk in that group. It can also affect impulse control in some people, such as increased gambling or other urges — let your doctor know if this happens.
typical_dosing: Doses vary depending on what it is being used for. For adults, starting doses are typically 10–15 mg once a day by mouth for schizophrenia or bipolar disorder. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on how you respond. It can be taken with or without food. There is also a long-acting injectable version given by a healthcare provider once a month if daily pills are not preferred.
